GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Prabumulih. 2. City Government is the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 4. Vice Mayor is the Vice Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Council of the City of Prabumulih. 6. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 7. Office of Population Control, Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPPPA, is the Office of Population Control, Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih. 8. Regional General Hospital, hereinafter abbreviated as RSUD, is the Regional General Hospital (RSUD) of the City of Prabumulih. 9. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih. 10. Community-Based Integrated Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM, is Community-Based Integrated Protection (PATBM) of the City of Prabumulih. 11. Community Health Center, hereinafter abbreviated as Puskesmas, is the Community Health Center (Puskesmas) of the City of Prabumulih. 12. Regional Technical Implementation Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD, is the Technical Implementation element of the Office that carries out Technical Operational activities and/or certain Technical Supporting Activities. 13. Private is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Legal Entity Individuals who carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih. 14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 17. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 19. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 20. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 21. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 22. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 23. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 24. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 32.

Article 16
(1) The City Government in efforts to Protect women and children is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children,
b. making efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children including criminal acts of human trafficking,
c. improving the effectiveness of services for women and children victims of acts of Violence,
d. increasing efforts to Protect female workers,
e. strengthening and developing institutions providing Protection services for women and children,
f. conducting cooperation with the Government, other Regional Governments, private parties, business sectors and/or NGOs in efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, and
g. involving the active role of families, customary leaders, religious leaders, communities, and institutions in the field of Protection of women and children.
(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to Protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions and may coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 18
Protection of women and children victims of acts of Violence (1) is implemented through integrated services.
The provision of integrated services to women and children victims of acts (2) of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) uses the principles of:
a. gender responsive,
b. non-discrimination,
c. equal and respectful relations,
d. maintaining confidentiality, providing a sense of security and comfort,
e. respecting individual differences, non-judgmental,
f. respecting the choices and decisions of victims,
h. sensitive to the background and condition of victims and the use of language that is appropriate and understood by victims,
j. fast and simple,
k. empathy, and
l. fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

Article 68
The family, in efforts to protect the rights of women, has the role of: protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades human dignity, providing equal opportunities to women and children
a. to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural matters; and
b. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 25
(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and child victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and child victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
   a. their lives are threatened,
   b. receiving rejection from family or community,
   c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away, and/or
   d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity towards women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and child victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
   a. women and child victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
   b. women and child victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

SANCTIONS
Article 73
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and Children resulting in the occurrence of violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
If officials appointed to implement protection fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanisms.
Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with these regulations shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Part Four Social Rehabilitation
Article 23
Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter (1) is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women and children victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.
Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes (2) services: psychosocial motivation and diagnosis,
a. care and nurturing,
b. vocational training and entrepreneurship development,
c. mental and spiritual guidance,
d. physical guidance,
e. social guidance and psychosocial counseling,
f. accessibility services,
g. social assistance and aid,
h. resocialization guidance,
i. follow-up guidance, and/or
k. referral.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions in the social field,
b. Regional Apparatus that oversees Women's and Children's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centre(s) or existing social community organizations, or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Article 21
Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency/department in charge of the protection of women and children, as well as officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint-handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 19 letter [specify letter] constitutes an action by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims. Law enforcement services and legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 53
(1) The implementation of social welfare is directed towards:
a. individuals,
b. families,
c. groups; and/or
d. communities.
(2) The implementation of social welfare as referred to in paragraph (1) is prioritized for those who have lives that are not decent from a humanitarian perspective and have social problem criteria:
a. poverty,
b. neglect,
c. disability,
d. remoteness,
e. social dysfunction and behavioral deviation,
f. disaster victims; and/or
g. victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination.
(3) Social welfare as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of service provision:
a. health,
b. education,
c. legal aid,
d. assistance,
e. social, mental and spiritual guidance,
f. social rehabilitation; and/or
g. reintegration.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
General

MAYOR OF PRABUMULIH
PROVINCE OF SOUTH SUMATRA
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PRABUMULIH CITY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD THE MAYOR OF PRABUMULIH, Considering In view of

a. that to guarantee Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in accordance with their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and to receive Protection from Violence and other violations, legal certainty is necessary;

b. that to provide legal certainty in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as to carry out mandatory regional government affairs, regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation is necessary;

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 31
The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The City Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards,
b. technical guidance and training,
c. provision of facilities,
d. monitoring, and
e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of empowerment and the Protection of women and Child victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 28
Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing (1) assistance and Protection for women and children victims of acts of Violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
Types of legal aid services include: (2)
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports,
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office,
c. legal aid in the examination process at court,
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision, and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The City Government provides legal aid to women and children victims of acts of Violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) (4) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Fourth Part Health and Social
Article 48
(1) The City Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking.
(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are obligated to make efforts so that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 65
Service efforts carried out by the City Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for Child victims of acts of Violence.

Article 46
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 29
Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.
(1)
The repatriation of women and children victims of acts of Violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 73
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and Children resulting in the occurrence of violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The City Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards,
b. technical guidance and training,
c. provision of facilities,
d. monitoring, and
e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of empowerment and the Protection of women and Child victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 62
In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of the Child-Friendly City (KLA) policy in the Region, a (1) KLA Task Force is established.
The establishment and membership composition of the KLA Task Force is stipulated (2) by the Mayor's Decision.
The KLA Task Force is domiciled at the DPPKBPPPA Office.
(3) The KLA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), has the principal tasks (4):
a. coordinating the implementation of the KLA policy and development,
b. conducting socialization, advocacy and communication of information and education on the KLA policy,
c. collecting baseline data for KLA development,
d. conducting needs analysis sourced from baseline data,
e. conducting dissemination of baseline data,
f. determining the focus and priority of programs in realizing KLA, which are adjusted to regional potential,
g. preparing a (five) year Child-Friendly City regional action plan and work mechanism, and
h. conducting monitoring, evaluation and reporting at least (once) a year.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is based on the principles of:
a. best interests of women and Children,
b. gender justice and gender equality,
c. local wisdom,
d. enforcement and legal certainty,
e. non-discrimination,
f. right to life, survival, and development,

This Regional Regulation aims to ensure the fulfillment of women's empowerment and child protection in the City:
a. as a guide in planning, policies and strategies for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; b. protecting and preventing women and Children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and Children, increasing the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; c. and as a legal umbrella for PD within the Government of the City of Prabumulih that oversees women's empowerment and child protection in order to provide assistance and support to women and child victims starting from investigation at the police, prosecution to trial in court. SANCTIONS
Article 73
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and Children resulting in the occurrence of violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
If officials appointed to implement protection fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanisms.
Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with these regulations shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 25
(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and child victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and child victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
   a. their lives are threatened,
   b. receiving rejection from family or community,
   c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away, and/or
   d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Fourth Part Health and Social
Article 48
(1) The City Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking.
(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are obligated to make efforts so that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter (1) is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women and children victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.
Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes (2) services: psychosocial motivation and diagnosis,
a. care and nurturing,
b. vocational training and entrepreneurship development,
c. mental and spiritual guidance,
d. physical guidance,
e. social guidance and psychosocial counseling,
f. accessibility services,
g. social assistance and aid,
h. resocialization guidance,
i. follow-up guidance, and/or
k. referral.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions in the social field,
b. Regional Apparatus that oversees Women's and Children's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centre(s) or existing social community organizations, or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Article 58
(1) Facilitation of the Child justice system includes criminal and civil justice. (2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes
a. provision of companions or Child volunteers at the time of examination by investigators,
b. provision of legal and psychological assistance services,
c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims,
d. realizing restorative justice processes for Children in conflict with the law, and
e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.
(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal assistance services during the judicial process.

Article 53
(1) The implementation of social welfare is directed towards:
a. individuals,
b. families,
c. groups; and/or
d. communities.

a. poverty,
b. neglect,
c. disability,
d. remoteness,
e. social dysfunction and behavioral deviation,
f. disaster victims; and/or
g. victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

a. health,
b. education,
c. legal aid,
d. assistance,
e. social, mental and spiritual guidance,
f. social rehabilitation; and/or
g. reintegration.

Article 18
Protection of women and children victims of acts of Violence (1) is implemented through integrated services.

a. gender responsive,
b. non-discrimination,
c. equal and respectful relations,
d. maintaining confidentiality, providing a sense of security and comfort,
e. respecting individual differences, non-judgmental,
f. respecting the choices and decisions of victims,
h. sensitive to the background and condition of victims and the use of language that is appropriate and understood by victims,
j. fast and simple,
k. empathy, and
l. fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

a. that to guarantee Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in accordance with their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and to receive Protection from Violence and other violations, legal certainty is necessary;

b. that to provide legal certainty in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as to carry out mandatory regional government affairs, regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation is necessary;

Article 19 letter [specify letter] constitutes an action by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims. Law enforcement services and legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 16
(1) The City Government in efforts to Protect women and children is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children,
b. making efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children including criminal acts of human trafficking,
c. improving the effectiveness of services for women and children victims of acts of Violence,
d. increasing efforts to Protect female workers,
e. strengthening and developing institutions providing Protection services for women and children,
f. conducting cooperation with the Government, other Regional Governments, private parties, business sectors and/or NGOs in efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, and
g. involving the active role of families, customary leaders, religious leaders, communities, and institutions in the field of Protection of women and children.
(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to Protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions and may coordinate with relevant agencies.

Part One
General Article (1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity: b. improving Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capability in the fields of: 1. politics:
2. law:
3. social:
4. economy: and
5. culture.
c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.
(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 28
Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing (1) assistance and Protection for women and children victims of acts of Violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
Types of legal aid services include: (2)
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports,
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office,
c. legal aid in the examination process at court,
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision, and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The City Government provides legal aid to women and children victims of acts of Violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) (4) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 31
The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 21
Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency/department in charge of the protection of women and children, as well as officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint-handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Prabumulih. 2. City Government is the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 4. Private is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Legal Entity Individuals who carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih. 14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 17. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 19. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. b. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 18
Protection of women and children victims of acts of Violence (1) is implemented through integrated services.
The provision of integrated services to women and children victims of acts (2) of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) uses the principles of:
a. gender responsive,
b. non-discrimination,
c. equal and respectful relations,
d. maintaining confidentiality, providing a sense of security and comfort,
e. respecting individual differences, non-judgmental,
f. respecting the choices and decisions of victims,
h. sensitive to the background and condition of victims and the use of language that is appropriate and understood by victims,
j. fast and simple,
k. empathy, and
l. fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

Article 25
(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and child victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and child victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The City Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards,
b. technical guidance and training,
c. provision of facilities,
d. monitoring, and
e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of empowerment and the Protection of women and Child victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 62
In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of the Child-Friendly City (KLA) policy in the Region, a (1) KLA Task Force is established.
The establishment and membership composition of the KLA Task Force is stipulated (2) by the Mayor's Decision.
The KLA Task Force is domiciled at the DPPKBPPPA Office.
(3) The KLA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), has the principal tasks (4):
a. coordinating the implementation of the KLA policy and development,
b. conducting socialization, advocacy and communication of information and education on the KLA policy,
c. collecting baseline data for KLA development,
d. conducting needs analysis sourced from baseline data,
e. conducting dissemination of baseline data,
f. determining the focus and priority of programs in realizing KLA, which are adjusted to regional potential,
g. preparing a (five) year Child-Friendly City regional action plan and work mechanism, and
h. conducting monitoring, evaluation and reporting at least (once) a year.

Article 21
Complaints regarding acts of violence against women and children may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency/department in charge of the protection of women and children, as well as officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint-handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Four Social Rehabilitation
Article 23
Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter (1) is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women and children victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.
Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes (2) services: psychosocial motivation and diagnosis,
a. care and nurturing,
b. vocational training and entrepreneurship development,
c. mental and spiritual guidance,
d. physical guidance,
e. social guidance and psychosocial counseling,
f. accessibility services,
g. social assistance and aid,
h. resocialization guidance,
i. follow-up guidance, and/or
k. referral.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions in the social field,
b. Regional Apparatus that oversees Women's and Children's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centre(s) or existing social community organizations, or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Article 46
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and child victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
   a. women and child victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
   b. women and child victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

a. that to guarantee Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in accordance with their dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and to receive Protection from Violence and other violations, legal certainty is necessary;

Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 33. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 34. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 35. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 36. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 37. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 38. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood family in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 39. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to another generation as heritage, so strong is its integration with community behavior patterns. Article
The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is based on the principles of:
a. best interests of women and Children,
b. gender justice and gender equality,
c. local wisdom,
d. enforcement and legal certainty,
e. non-discrimination,
f. right to life, survival, and development,
g. respect for Children's opinions. Article
This Regional Regulation aims to ensure the fulfillment of women's empowerment and child protection in the City:
a. as a guide in planning, policies and strategies for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; b. protecting and preventing women and Children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and Children, increasing the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; c. and as a legal umbrella for PD within the Government of the City of Prabumulih that oversees women's empowerment and child protection in order to provide assistance and support to women and child victims starting from investigation at the police, prosecution to trial in court. Article
The scope of regulation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection includes:
a. protection of women; b. protection of Children; c. fulfillment of Children's rights; d. improvement of quality of life of women and children; e. community participation; and
f. guidance, supervision, assistance. g. gender and child data system, disaggregated data on women and children. CHAPTER II
IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

SANCTIONS
Article 73
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and Children resulting in the occurrence of violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
If officials appointed to implement protection fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanisms.
Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with these regulations shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Part Four Social Rehabilitation
Article 23
Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter (1) is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women and children victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.
Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes (2) services: psychosocial motivation and diagnosis,
a. care and nurturing,
b. vocational training and entrepreneurship development,
c. mental and spiritual guidance,
d. physical guidance,
e. social guidance and psychosocial counseling,
f. accessibility services,
g. social assistance and aid,
h. resocialization guidance,
i. follow-up guidance, and/or
k. referral.

a. Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions in the social field,

Article 53
(1) The implementation of social welfare is directed towards:
a. individuals,
b. families,
c. groups; and/or
d. communities.

a. poverty,
b. neglect,
c. disability,
d. remoteness,
e. social dysfunction and behavioral deviation,
f. disaster victims; and/or
g. victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

a. health,
b. education,
c. legal aid,
d. assistance,
e. social, mental and spiritual guidance,
f. social rehabilitation; and/or
g. reintegration.

Article 42
(1) The City Government, in efforts to protect and fulfill the rights of Children, is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies and programs/activities for the protection and fulfillment of Children's rights,
b. respecting and guaranteeing the human rights of every Child without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, the legal status of the Child, the birth order of the Child, and physical and/or mental condition,
c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in realizing Children's rights,
d. guaranteeing the Protection, care, and welfare of Children with due regard to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, or other persons legally responsible for the Child,

g. conducting supervision and guidance in the context of implementation, and
h. conducting cooperation with private parties in the implementation of Child Protection.

SANCTIONS
Article 73
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and Children resulting in the occurrence of violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
If officials appointed to implement protection fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanisms.
Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with these regulations shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 58
(1) Facilitation of the Child justice system includes criminal and civil justice. (2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes
a. provision of companions or Child volunteers at the time of examination by investigators,
b. provision of legal and psychological assistance services,
c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims,
d. realizing restorative justice processes for Children in conflict with the law, and
e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.
(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal assistance services during the judicial process.
(4) In facilitating the Child justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized PD is the PD responsible for women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and child perpetrators, in police examinations, at the prosecutor's office, and in court.

Article 19 letter [specify letter] constitutes an action by law enforcement officials to implement statutory regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims. Law enforcement services and legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 28
Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing (1) assistance and Protection for women and children victims of acts of Violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
Types of legal aid services include: (2)
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports,
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office,
c. legal aid in the examination process at court,
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision, and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The City Government provides legal aid to women and children victims of acts of Violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) (4) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 16
(1) The City Government in efforts to Protect women and children is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children,
b. making efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children including criminal acts of human trafficking,
c. improving the effectiveness of services for women and children victims of acts of Violence,
d. increasing efforts to Protect female workers,
e. strengthening and developing institutions providing Protection services for women and children,
f. conducting cooperation with the Government, other Regional Governments, private parties, business sectors and/or NGOs in efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, and
g. involving the active role of families, customary leaders, religious leaders, communities, and institutions in the field of Protection of women and children.
(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to Protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions and may coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and child victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
   a. women and child victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
   b. women and child victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

(1) The City Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.

(1) The role of community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

Article 18
Protection of women and children victims of acts of Violence (1) is implemented through integrated services.
The provision of integrated services to women and children victims of acts (2) of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) uses the principles of:
a. gender responsive,
b. non-discrimination,
c. equal and respectful relations,
d. maintaining confidentiality, providing a sense of security and comfort,
e. respecting individual differences, non-judgmental,
f. respecting the choices and decisions of victims,
h. sensitive to the background and condition of victims and the use of language that is appropriate and understood by victims,
j. fast and simple,
k. empathy, and
l. fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

Article 23
Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter (1) is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women and children victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.
Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes (2) services: psychosocial motivation and diagnosis,
a. care and nurturing,
b. vocational training and entrepreneurship development,
c. mental and spiritual guidance,
d. physical guidance,
e. social guidance and psychosocial counseling,
f. accessibility services,
g. social assistance and aid,
h. resocialization guidance,
i. follow-up guidance, and/or
k. referral.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions in the social field,
b. Regional Apparatus that oversees Women's and Children's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centre(s) or existing social community organizations, or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Fourth Part Health and Social
Article 48
(1) The City Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking.
(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are obligated to make efforts so that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 16

Article 25

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and child victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
   a. women and child victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
   b. women and child victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

Article 73

Article 42
(1) The City Government, in efforts to protect and fulfill the rights of Children, is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies and programs/activities for the protection and fulfillment of Children's rights,
b. respecting and guaranteeing the human rights of every Child without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, the legal status of the Child, the birth order of the Child, and physical and/or mental condition,

Article 66
(1) The role of community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children:
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
(2) The community, parents and families are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and child victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
   a. women and child victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
   b. women and child victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 58
(1) Facilitation of the Child justice system includes criminal and civil justice. (2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes
a. provision of companions or Child volunteers at the time of examination by investigators,
b. provision of legal and psychological assistance services,
c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims,
d. realizing restorative justice processes for Children in conflict with the law, and
e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.
(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal assistance services during the judicial process.
(4) In facilitating the Child justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized PD is the PD responsible for women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and child perpetrators, in police examinations, at the prosecutor's office, and in court.

Article 53
(1) The implementation of social welfare is directed towards:
a. individuals,
b. families,
c. groups; and/or
d. communities.
(2) The implementation of social welfare as referred to in paragraph (1) is prioritized for those who have lives that are not decent from a humanitarian perspective and have social problem criteria:
a. poverty,
b. neglect,
c. disability,
d. remoteness,
e. social dysfunction and behavioral deviation,
f. disaster victims; and/or
g. victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination.
(3) Social welfare as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of service provision:
a. health,
b. education,
c. legal aid,
d. assistance,
e. social, mental and spiritual guidance,
f. social rehabilitation; and/or
g. reintegration.

Article
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Prabumulih. 2. City Government is the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 4. Vice Mayor is the Vice Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Council of the City of Prabumulih. 6. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 7. Office of Population Control, Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPPPA, is the Office of Population Control, Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih. 8. Regional General Hospital, hereinafter abbreviated as RSUD, is the Regional General Hospital (RSUD) of the City of Prabumulih. 9. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih. 10. Community-Based Integrated Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM, is Community-Based Integrated Protection (PATBM) of the City of Prabumulih. 11. Community Health Center, hereinafter abbreviated as Puskesmas, is the Community Health Center (Puskesmas) of the City of Prabumulih. 12. Regional Technical Implementation Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD, is the Technical Implementation element of the Office that carries out Technical Operational activities and/or certain Technical Supporting Activities. 13. Private is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Legal Entity Individuals who carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih. 14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 17. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 19. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 20. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 21. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 22. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 23. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 24. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 32.

Article
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Prabumulih. 2. City Government is the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 4. Regional Technical Implementation Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD, is the Technical Implementation element of the Office that carries out Technical Operational activities and/or certain Technical Supporting Activities. 13. Private is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Legal Entity Individuals who carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih. 14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 17. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 19. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 20. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 21. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 22. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 23. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 24. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 32.

Private is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Legal Entity Individuals who carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih. 14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 17. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 19. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 20. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 21. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 22. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 23. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 24. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 32.

Article 28
Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing (1) assistance and Protection for women and children victims of acts of Violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
Types of legal aid services include: (2)
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports,
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office,
c. legal aid in the examination process at court,
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision, and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The City Government provides legal aid to women and children victims of acts of Violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) (4) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 62
In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of the Child-Friendly City (KLA) policy in the Region, a (1) KLA Task Force is established.
The establishment and membership composition of the KLA Task Force is stipulated (2) by the Mayor's Decision.
The KLA Task Force is domiciled at the DPPKBPPPA Office.
(3) The KLA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), has the principal tasks (4):
a. coordinating the implementation of the KLA policy and development,
b. conducting socialization, advocacy and communication of information and education on the KLA policy,
c. collecting baseline data for KLA development,
d. conducting needs analysis sourced from baseline data,
e. conducting dissemination of baseline data,
f. determining the focus and priority of programs in realizing KLA, which are adjusted to regional potential,
g. preparing a (five) year Child-Friendly City regional action plan and work mechanism, and
h. conducting monitoring, evaluation and reporting at least (once) a year.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 10
(1) The Technical Team as referred to in Article ... letter ... shall consist of officials who understand gender-responsive budget analysis as well as Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) The regional action plan for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as referred to in Article ... letter ... shall contain: a. women's empowerment and child protection in laws and regulations in the City,
b. women's empowerment and child protection in the development cycle in the City,
c. institutional strengthening of women's empowerment and child protection in the City, and
d. strengthening community participation in the City.

Article 16
(1) The City Government in efforts to Protect women and children is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children,
b. making efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children including criminal acts of human trafficking,
c. improving the effectiveness of services for women and children victims of acts of Violence,
d. increasing efforts to Protect female workers,
e. strengthening and developing institutions providing Protection services for women and children,
f. conducting cooperation with the Government, other Regional Governments, private parties, business sectors and/or NGOs in efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, and
g. involving the active role of families, customary leaders, religious leaders, communities, and institutions in the field of Protection of women and children.
(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to Protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions and may coordinate with relevant agencies.

Fourth Part Health and Social
Article 48
(1) The City Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking.
(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are obligated to make efforts so that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.
